items.title: Professor Longhair (Henry Roeland Byrd) Interview, 1975-11-13
items.q: Smokey Johnson, and Honey Boy, oh I can name a bunch of them, you know, Drummer, Sheva, all of them, you know.

ctx.x: He was just probably the A&R man, like they said. Yeah. Yeah. Did you have any, at that time, did you have any special people you used on your sessions?

No, I let them do all the picking. I let them do all the picking. I let them do all the picking. Just like it is now with me with Quince. I don't pick them because it's a headache. I got tired of that many years ago. You know, first of all you pick a guy and he develops what you're trying to learn, and he don't never stay no way. They get ideas of their own. It ain't waste teaching to show it nobody, not in the field in that manner, you know. Smokey Johnson, and Honey Boy, oh I can name a bunch of them, you know,…
Yeah, well you work with Honey Boy, I know. Yeah. Tali Otis, this is me.
